repository_discipline.rationale: Hydra owns task and Reward selection; environment code retains dispatch; scripts remain assembly-only.

dimensions.name: responsibility-ownership
dimensions.evidence: One Hydra profile owns branch membership and scales; existing RewardModeConfig owns dispatch; Oracle preflight owns admission.

dimensions.name: public-interface
dimensions.evidence: The change consumes existing RewardModeConfig, reward function registry, and Hydra composition interfaces.

dimensions.name: dependency-direction
dimensions.evidence: The SAC runtime validates resolved config and does not reach into backend or environment-private state.

dimensions.name: state-lifecycle
dimensions.evidence: Reward identity is sealed in existing Oracle config hashes; no new mutable state is introduced.

dimensions.name: change-surface
dimensions.evidence: One config profile plus one structural validator replaces the old prohibition without adding a second route.

dimensions.name: evidence-boundary
dimensions.evidence: Offline tests prove config and dispatch semantics but explicitly do not claim policy quality.

dimensions.name: proof-route
dimensions.evidence: RED tests cover valid composition, missing support ownership, gait aliases, enabled gait constraint, and mode-disabled overrides.

dimensions.name: tensor-provenance
dimensions.evidence: Actor observation remains unchanged at deployable 98-D plus the existing privileged bundle.

dimensions.name: gradient-update-boundary
dimensions.evidence: The change affects Reward configuration and preflight only; optimizer ownership is unchanged.

dimensions.name: persistence-evaluation
dimensions.evidence: Existing canonical reward config hashing binds the new Reward identity to checkpoints.

dimensions.name: repository-discipline
dimensions.evidence: Config-first and owner-layer rules are preserved; no backend or script leakage is introduced.

residual_risks.description: Offline construction cannot prove SAC convergence or stable stand/walk behavior.
residual_risks.disposition: Require formal runtime and policy-quality audits before admitting a trained Oracle.
